note: Display decisions for the page that the data cannot make by rule. Each one follows from the row's `caution` in liston/witnesses.json; `why` quotes or paraphrases it. Keys under `witnesses` are QIDs.
tagline: Trombonist, arranger and composer — the first woman trombonist to play alongside men in the big bands.
tagline_source: Reworded from the first paragraph of her Wikipedia article. The mockup's line ('the first woman to hold a chair in the great bebop big bands') is a wider claim than any source in this repo makes.

Q601523.why: J. C. Higginbotham. The only quotable line is '(That boy) can play some trombone!', an uncertain transcription about a woman the interviewer calls 'Melvin Liston'. Caution: 'display with care or not at all'.

Q270893.why: Shirley Horn. Stance is mixed: quoting only 'a great jazz artist' would misrepresent her. The second quote carries the reservation.

Q231071.note: Said while dismissing women in jazz generally; Liston is her exception.
Q231071.why: Abbey Lincoln. The line sits inside a strongly anti-feminist passage; the caution asks for a note on context.

Q1102326.note: Said to Liston, as her interviewer, in 1996.
Q1102326.why: Clora Bryant is the interviewer in Liston's own oral history, not the subject of one.

Q1691660.note: Speaking as co-interviewer in Clark Terry’s oral history.
Q1691660.why: Joe Williams is not the interviewee of the transcript the card links to.

Q126677.note: Williams calls her only “Melba”, and is reporting what she was told.
Q126677.why: Mary Lou Williams. Identification rests on context; the quoted words are second-hand.
